Component Prototype Builder helps designers build VA-ready prototypes built with real VADS components and standards. Move quickly into user testing with smart engineering review. Once user testing succeeds, push your prototype to Figma for finalizing.

The Challenge

Every prototype gets built, reviewed and rebuilt, and every round costs the team time.

Designers and engineers work from different artifacts, so gaps surface late.

Feasibility is answered after the design is built, so user testing slips a cycle.

Approved work is rebuilt by hand in Figma.

The Oddball Solution

Meet Component Prototype Builder: quickly build VA-ready prototypes ready for user testing.

  • Quickly draft prototypes in a shared space, ready for user testing.
  • Build pages from templates, or use the custom builder to describe your vision.
  • Easily save and send for engineering review.
  • After successful user testing, push your prototype to Figma for fine tuning and sprint completion.
How Designers Build

Designers do most of their work in Pages, and reach for two builders when they need more.

Pages. The composer, where designers arrange each page. Start from a template, add as many pages as you need, and let the checks run as you go.

Components. For something more specific than a standard VADS component. Describe it, refine it, then save it for use in the Pages composer.

Forms. Same idea for forms. Describe one, get chapters and pages that follow VA forms patterns, then save it for Pages.

Know What VA.gov Uses

Designers see how VA.gov already uses each component.

Where it is used. The products that use each component.

States. Each state, shown with the real VA web components.

Accessibility. Guidance for each component.

Props and code. The markup, ready to copy.

How Engineers Review

Engineers weigh in before user testing, with what they need to decide.

Specs. The components, layout and states behind each page.

Data. Where each value comes from, set field by field. Anything left on its default becomes a question.

Go or no-go. Mark each system feasible or not, answer open questions, then work through changes with the designer to a go or no-go before anything reaches user testing.

Zero To Prototype Kit

Four steps from zero to a VA Prototype Kit bundle, ready for user testing.

Step 1 of 4

Compose

Arrange your pages in the composer, from templates and VADS parts.

Step 2 of 4

Customize

Need something more specific? Build a component or form and save it for Pages.

Step 3 of 4

Review

Send it to your engineer, then work through changes together to a go or no-go.

Step 4 of 4

Export

Download the VA Prototype Kit bundle. When the prototype is ready, the designer moves it to the VA Prototype GitHub for user testing.

Send It To Figma

When user testing comes back successful, push the prototype to Figma.

Designers fine tune and finalize for the sprint instead of rebuilding, so the whole team redoes less.

What It Checks For You

Mistakes show up while you build, not at review.

Heading order, spacing on the VADS scale and VADS-only parts are checked as designers work. A skipped heading level is flagged with a one-click fix, so engineering reviews a cleaner prototype.

Designers, engineers and product teams work from one prototype. Engineering weighs in first, so a VA-ready prototype reaches user testing faster and Figma gets less rework.
